primary_issue: Severe overexposure / highlight clipping: large areas blow out to pure white, destroying readability of the water (spray + puddle) and cabinet materials.
issues: Massive highlight clipping/overexposure across water and cabinet surfaces; specular/refraction detail is lost.
Spray and puddle are not clearly readable; fine droplets/mist are indistinguishable against blown-out background.
Water shading does not read as clear refractive liquid (IOR/refraction cues largely absent due to clipping; appears as overbright blobs).
Weak/unclear interaction with cabinet wall/floor (wetting, rivulets, contact darkening/spec changes are not convincingly visible).
Visible meshing/stepping artifacts and hard-edged blobs suggest low effective sim/mesh resolution and/or domain boundary cutoff.
Scale feels off: jet thickness and droplet sizes appear too large relative to cabinet plumbing (hard to judge precisely because exposure masks detail).
Color management/tonemapping appears incorrect (looks like raw/linear with clipped highs), reducing realism and contrast in indirect-lit cabinet space.
suggestions: Fix exposure/tonemapping before changing sim: reduce overall exposure by ~2–3 stops and ensure a filmic/managed view transform so highlights roll off instead of clipping.
Render to EXR and inspect raw values; avoid destructive clipping. If needed, clamp only indirect/specular carefully to prevent fireflies without flattening reflections.

Increase liquid sim/mesh fidelity to remove blockiness: raise domain resolution_max (e.g., 96→128+) and ensure meshing is enabled with sufficient smoothing; verify timesteps_max/substeps are high enough to avoid discretized jet stepping.
Increase/expand the liquid domain bounds so splashes/stream never touch or cut against the domain walls (prevents straight cutoffs).
Make water physically readable: set water IOR ~1.33, strong transmission with low roughness; add subtle absorption (slight blue tint) so thickness reads while staying clear.
Add a wet-look treatment on cabinet wood/floor at contact points (darken + increase specular / reduce roughness locally) so runoff and puddle contact sells the leak.
If the spray still reads too “chunky,” reduce emitter thickness and/or increase substeps; consider adding a secondary particle/mist pass for fine droplets and motion-blurred streaks.
Add mild motion blur and keep DOF moderate so droplets streak slightly while the burst fitting remains sharp (helps sell speed and scale).
vision_assessment: The shot composition communicates an under-sink leak setup, but the render is dominated by extreme overexposure: broad regions of the cabinet interior and the fluid render as pure white, eliminating the very cues that make water believable (specular highlights with roll-off, refraction distortion, caustic-like brightening, and thickness/absorption). The water is present, but the spray fan and puddle are hard to parse; detail in droplets and ripples is largely lost. Where the fluid is visible (notably near the bottom/right), the liquid reads somewhat blobby/blocky, suggesting insufficient resolution/meshing and possible domain/boundary influence. Overall, the effect does not yet convincingly read as a pressurized sideways hose burst with established puddling and runoff because exposure and stepping artifacts prevent material and motion readability.
